node_actin_cortex.title: Actin Microfilaments (G-Actin to F-Actin)
node_actin_cortex.subtitle: 7 nm Polarized Helical Filaments | Lamellipodia, Filopodia & Stress Fibers

metrics.monomer_unit: 42 kDa Globular Actin (G-Actin) containing a tightly bound ATP + Mg2+/Ca2+
metrics.structural_polarity: Barbed (+) End (Fast growing) vs. Pointed (-) End (Slow growing)

mechanism: Globular G-actin monomers polymerize head-to-tail into two protofilaments that twist around each other in a right-handed helix (repeating every 37 nm) to form Filamentous F-actin.

Controlled globally by the Rho family of small monomeric GTPases (CSIR Classic): **Cdc42** triggers thin spike-like **Filopodia**; **Rac1** triggers broad sheet-like **Lamellipodia**; **RhoA** triggers contractile **Stress Fibers** and focal adhesion assembly.
csir_high_yield: Arrowhead Decoration Experiment (CSIR Part B/C Staple): Incubating F-actin with Myosin S1 subfragments (in the absence of ATP) coats the filament with distinctive arrowheads: the **Pointed (-) end** corresponds to the tip of the arrowhead, while the **Barbed (+) end** corresponds to the notched base!
Rho GTPase Triumvirate: Memorize Cdc42 = Filopodia (chemotactic sensing); Rac = Lamellipodia (membrane ruffling); RhoA = Stress fibers (actomyosin contraction via ROCK kinase).
pathology: Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome (WAS): X-linked mutation in the WASP protein (which connects Cdc42-GTP to the Arp2/3 actin nucleator) causes defective actin polymerization in T-cells and platelets, resulting in eczema, microthrombocytopenia, and immunodeficiency.
lab_workbench: Fluorescent Phalloidin Staining (Alexa Fluor 488-Phalloidin): Binds specifically at the interface between F-actin subunits (ignoring monomeric G-actin), providing high-contrast visualization of the actin cytoskeleton in fixed cells.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (3J8I — Near-Atomic Cryo-EM Structure of the F-Actin Filament)

node_microtubule_network.title: Microtubules (13-Protofilament Hollow Cylinders)
node_microtubule_network.subtitle: 25 nm Rigid Hollow Tubes | α/β-Tubulin Heterodimers & Organelle Highways

metrics.diameter: 25 nm outer diameter (~15 nm hollow lumen)
metrics.protofilament_geometry: 13 linear protofilaments arranged in parallel around a hollow core (Singlet MT)
metrics.monomer_unit: α/β-Tubulin Heterodimer (~110 kDa; α-tubulin binds non-exchangeable GTP; β-tubulin binds exchangeable GTP/GDP)

mechanism: Obligate α/β-tubulin heterodimers align longitudinally head-to-tail into protofilaments. Lateral interactions between 13 protofilaments close into a rigid hollow cylinder with a high persistence length.

Displays strict intrinsic polarity: **α-tubulin** is exposed at the slow-growing **Minus (-) end** (typically anchored at the centrosome), while **β-tubulin** is exposed at the fast-growing **Plus (+) end** radiating toward the cell periphery.
csir_high_yield: The Non-Exchangeable (N-site) vs. Exchangeable (E-site) GTP Rule: GTP bound to **α-tubulin** (N-site) is buried at the intradimer interface and is NEVER hydrolyzed! Only GTP bound to **β-tubulin** (E-site) at the interdimer interface is hydrolyzed to GDP shortly after incorporation into the microtubule lattice.

Singlet vs. Doublet vs. Triplet Architecture: Cytoplasmic/mitotic microtubules are **Singlets (13 protofilaments)**; Cilia and Flagella axonemes contain **9 Outer Doublets + 2 Central Singlets (9+2)** where the A-tubule has 13 protofilaments and the incomplete B-tubule has 10–11; Basal bodies and Centrioles contain **9 Triplets (9+0)**.
pathology: Alzheimer's Disease & Tauopathies: Hyperphosphorylation of the microtubule-associated protein **Tau** (which normally stabilizes axonal microtubules) causes Tau to detach from microtubules and aggregate into neurofibrillary tangles, leading to axonal transport collapse.
lab_workbench: Cold-Induced Depolymerization & Taxol Stabilization Assay: Cooling mammalian cells or purified microtubules to 4°C (or adding millimolar Ca2+) triggers rapid depolymerization into α/β dimers, unless stabilized by Taxol or MAPs.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (1JFF — Refined Atomic Structure of Alpha-Beta Tubulin Dimer bound to Taxol)
OMIM Database (MAPT / Tau Mutations in Frontotemporal Dementia)

node_intermediate_filaments.title: Intermediate Filaments (10 nm Rope-Like Mechanical Cables)
node_intermediate_filaments.subtitle: Apolar Staggered Tetramer Assembly | Zero Nucleotide Binding & Zero Motor Proteins

metrics.diameter: ~10 nm (Intermediate between 7 nm Actin and 25 nm Microtubules)
metrics.structural_polarity: APOLAR (Symmetric ends due to antiparallel staggered tetramer assembly)
metrics.nucleotide_requirement: NONE (Does not bind ATP or GTP; spontaneous self-assembly)

mechanism: Unlike globular actin and tubulin, Intermediate Filament (IF) monomers are elongated fibrous proteins with a conserved central α-helical rod domain flanked by variable globular head and tail domains.

ASSEMBLY HIERARCHY: Two monomers twist in **parallel** into a coiled-coil dimer \rightarrow Two dimers associate in an **ANTIPARALLEL, staggered** manner to form an **apolar tetramer** (the soluble fundamental subunit) \rightarrow 8 tetramers pack laterally into a unit-length filament that anneals end-to-end into a tough 10 nm rope.
csir_high_yield: Why are there NO motor proteins that walk on Intermediate Filaments? (Classic CSIR NET Conceptual Question): Because two parallel coiled-coil dimers associate in an ANTIPARALLEL orientation to form the tetramer, both ends of the final filament are chemically and structurally identical (Apolar)! Without structural polarity (+ and - ends), directional motor movement is physically impossible.
Tissue-Specific IF Classification (Used in Tumor Histopathology):
• **Type I & II**: Acidic & Basic **Keratins** (Epithelial cells; obligate heterodimers).
• **Type III**: **Vimentin** (Mesenchymal cells/fibroblasts), **Desmin** (Muscle cells), **GFAP** (Astrocytes/Glia).
• **Type IV**: **Neurofilaments** (NF-L, NF-M, NF-H in neuronal axons).
• **Type V**: **Nuclear Lamins** (Lamins A, B, C in all nucleated cells).
pathology: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex (EBS): Dominant-negative mutations in Keratin 5 or Keratin 14 disrupt the basal epidermal keratin network, causing severe skin blistering upon mild mechanical friction.
lab_workbench: High-Salt & Non-Ionic Detergent Extraction: When cells are extracted with 1% Triton X-100 and high salt (0.6 M KCl), actin and microtubules solubilize and wash away, leaving behind the insoluble Intermediate Filament cytoskeleton and nuclear lamina.

node_mtoc_centrosome.title: The Centrosome (MTOC) & γ-Tubulin Ring Complex (γ-TuRC)
node_mtoc_centrosome.subtitle: Orthogonal 9+0 Centriole Pair & Minus-End Nucleation Template

metrics.core_architecture: Mother & Daughter Centrioles (9 triplet microtubules in 9+0 cartwheel symmetry) surrounded by Pericentriolar Material (PCM)
metrics.nucleation_template: γ-Tubulin Ring Complex (γ-TuRC) — Cone-shaped lock-washer template of 13 γ-tubulin subunits
metrics.cartwheel_hub: SAS-6 protein oligomer (Enforces strict 9-fold radial symmetry of centrioles)

mechanism: Spontaneous nucleation of α/β-tubulin dimers in the cytosol is kinetically unfavorable. The Centrosome (Microtubule Organizing Center) overcomes this kinetic barrier using the Pericentriolar Material (PCM) studded with **γ-Tubulin Ring Complexes (γ-TuRCs)**.

γ-TuRC acts as a 13-subunit helical template that binds the α-tubulin face of incoming α/β-tubulin heterodimers, capping and anchoring the **Minus (-) end** at the centrosome while forcing the **Plus (+) end** to grow outward toward the plasma membrane.
csir_high_yield: Which cells LACK centrosomes/centrioles yet still form functional mitotic spindles? Higher plant cells and mammalian oocytes (during meiosis) completely lack centrioles! They nucleate microtubules via chromatin-mediated Ran-GTP pathways and acentrosomal γ-TuRC clusters.
PLK4 (Polo-Like Kinase 4) and SAS-6 are the master regulators of centriole duplication (occurring strictly once per cell cycle at the G1/S transition).
pathology: Primary Autosomal Recessive Microcephaly (MCPH): Mutations in centrosomal proteins (ASPM, CDK5RAP2, CENPJ) disrupt mitotic spindle orientation in neural progenitor cells, severely reducing cerebral cortex neuron numbers.
lab_workbench: Microtubule Regrowth (Nocodazole Washout) Assay: Cells treated with nocodazole depolymerize all cytoplasmic microtubules; within 60 seconds of drug washout, bright aster-like stars of new microtubules nucleate selectively from γ-tubulin foci at the centrosome.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (6V6S — Cryo-EM Structure of the Human Gamma-Tubulin Ring Complex)

metrics.monomer_regulators: Profilin (Promotes ADP->ATP exchange & + end addition) vs. Thymosin-β4 (Sequesters G-actin)

mechanism: In vitro polymerization follows a 3-phase sigmoidal curve: (1) **Lag/Nucleation Phase**: Rate-limiting formation of a stable G-actin trimer seed (can be bypassed by adding pre-formed F-actin seeds); (2) **Elongation Phase**: Rapid monomer addition to both ends (+ end grows ~5–10x faster than - end); (3) **Steady-State / Equilibrium Phase**.

TREADMILLING MECHANISM: Because ATP is hydrolyzed to ADP shortly after G-actin joins the filament, the (+) end is capped with high-affinity **ATP-actin** ($C_c^+ \approx 0.1\ \mu\text{M}$), while the (-) end exposes low-affinity **ADP-actin** ($C_c^- \approx 0.8\ \mu\text{M}$). When free cytosolic $[\text{G-actin}]$ lies between $0.1\ \mu\text{M}$ and $0.8\ \mu\text{M}$, net assembly occurs at the (+) end while net disassembly occurs at the (-) end at equal rates!
csir_high_yield: Critical Concentration ($C_c$) Inequality Rules (Guaranteed CSIR Part C Numerical/Graphical Question):
• If $[\text{Free Monomer}] < C_c^+$: **BOTH ends shrink** (No net polymerization).
• If $C_c^+ < [\text{Free Monomer}] < C_c^-$: **Plus (+) end grows while Minus (-) end shrinks** (**TREADMILLING!**).
• If $[\text{Free Monomer}] > C_c^-$: **BOTH ends grow** (+ end grows faster than - end).
Key Actin-Binding Proteins:
• **Cofilin / ADF**: Binds ADP-actin near the pointed (-) end, twisting and severing the filament to accelerate disassembly.
• **Profilin**: Binds ADP-G-actin, catalyzes nucleotide exchange to ATP-G-actin, and delivers it specifically to the barbed (+) end.
• **CapZ**: Caps the barbed (+) end; **Tropomodulin**: Caps the pointed (-) end.
pathology: Listeria monocytogenes Intracellular Rocket Tails: The pathogenic bacterium expresses the surface protein **ActA**, which mimics host WASP to hijack the host cell's Arp2/3 complex,Profilin, and Cofilin, polymerizing a comet tail of actin that propels the bacterium directly through the cytoplasm into neighboring cells!
lab_workbench: Pyrene-Labeled Actin Fluorimetry Assay: Pyrene covalently attached to Cys-374 of G-actin exhibits a 20-fold increase in fluorescence emission (at 407 nm) upon incorporation into F-actin, allowing real-time kinetic recording of the lag, elongation, and steady-state phases.

node_arp23_formin.title: Actin Nucleators: Arp2/3 (70° Branches) vs. Formins (Unbranched Cables)
node_arp23_formin.subtitle: Architectural Control of Branched Lamellipodial Meshworks vs. Linear Filopodia & Stress Fibers

metrics.arp23_geometry: Nucleates new filaments from the Minus (-) end at a strict 70° Y-branch angle off mother filaments
metrics.formin_geometry: Dimeric FH2 ring stays processively attached to the growing Barbed (+) end (Unbranched filaments)
metrics.crosslinkers: Filamin (V-shaped flexible gel meshwork) vs. Fimbrin & α-Actinin (Parallel bundles)

mechanism: **THE Arp2/3 COMPLEX (Branched Networks)**: Contains two actin-related proteins (Arp2 and Arp3) that structurally mimic a G-actin dimer. When activated by nucleation-promoting factors (**WASP / WAVE / Scar**) downstream of Rac1/Cdc42, Arp2/3 binds to the side of a pre-existing mother filament and nucleates a daughter filament at an exact **70° angle** (remaining capped at the pointed - end while the barbed + end grows forward to push the lamellipodium).

**FORMINS (Linear Unbranched Filaments)**: Activated by Rho-GTP, dimeric Formins use their donut-shaped **FH2 domain** to nucleate unbranched actin filaments and ride processively on the growing **Barbed (+) end** (while their proline-rich **FH1 domain** recruits Profilin-ATP-actin), protecting the (+) end from Capping Protein to build stress fibers, filopodia, and the cytokinetic contractile ring.
csir_high_yield: Arp2/3 vs. Formin Contrast (CSIR Part B/C Favorite):
• **Arp2/3**: Remains bound at the **Pointed (-) end**; creates **70° branched** dendritic networks (Lamellipodia).
• **Formins**: Remain processively bound at the **Barbed (+) end**; create **straight, unbranched** filaments (Filopodia, Stress fibers, Contractile ring).

Actin Bundling Spacer Rule: **Fimbrin** (monomeric, 14 nm spacing) packs parallel actin filaments so tightly in microvilli/filopodia that Myosin II CANNOT fit between them; **α-Actinin** (dimeric, 40 nm wider spacing) crosslinks antiparallel stress fibers with enough room for Myosin II motors to enter and contract!
pathology: Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis (FSGS): Mutations in INF2 (Inverted Formin 2) or ACTN4 (α-Actinin-4) disrupt podocyte foot process actin architecture in the kidney glomerulus, causing severe proteinuria and renal failure.
lab_workbench: Two-Color TIRF (Total Internal Reflection Fluorescence) Microscopy: Directly visualizes single Arp2/3 complexes landing on mother actin filaments and sprouting 70° daughter branches within a 100 nm evanescent field.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (4JD2 — Arp2/3 Complex Bound to Mother Actin Filament Branch Junction)
RCSB PDB (1Y64 — Formin FH2 Dimer Ring Complexed with Actin)

node_mt_dynamic_instability.title: Microtubule Dynamic Instability: The GTP Cap, Catastrophe & Rescue
node_mt_dynamic_instability.subtitle: Stochastic Switching Between Polymerization and Rapid Curved-Protofilament Peeling

metrics.gtp_cap: Straight α/β-GTP tubulin conformation at the growing Plus (+) tip stabilizes lateral contacts
metrics.catastrophe: Loss of GTP cap exposes curved GDP-tubulin -> rapid peeling/depolymerization ('ram's horns')
metrics.rescue: Regaining a fresh GTP-tubulin cap halts shrinkage and resumes growth

mechanism: Discovered by Tim Mitchison and Marc Kirschner: Individual microtubules at steady state undergo stochastic transitions between prolonged growth and rapid shrinkage (**Dynamic Instability**), allowing rapid 'search-and-capture' of kinetochores during mitosis.

**THE GTP CAP MODEL**: α/β-tubulin dimers bearing **GTP on β-tubulin** adopt a **straight conformation** that packs tightly into the cylindrical lattice (forming a stabilizing **GTP Cap** at the + end). Shortly after incorporation, β-tubulin hydrolyzes GTP to GDP. **GDP-tubulin** prefers a **curved/kinked conformation** (~12° bend), storing mechanical strain inside the lattice.

**CATASTROPHE vs. RESCUE**: If the rate of GTP hydrolysis catches up to and overtakes the rate of fresh GTP-dimer addition, the GTP cap is lost! Exposed GDP-protofilaments violently peel outward like curling ram's horns (**Catastrophe**). If fresh GTP-tubulin dimers recap the shrinking tip, depolymerization stops and growth resumes (**Rescue**).
csir_high_yield: Non-Hydrolyzable GTP Analog Experiment (GMPCPP / GTPγS — Classic CSIR Part C Question): What happens if microtubules are assembled in the presence of **GMPCPP** (a non-hydrolyzable GTP analog)? Microtubules polymerize rapidly, NEVER undergo catastrophe, and become completely stable because the straight 'GTP-cap' conformation extends throughout the entire polymer!
Plus-End Tracking & Catastrophe Regulators:
• **EB1 & XMAP215**: Plus-end tracking proteins (+TIPs) that promote rapid (+) end polymerization.
• **Kinesin-13 (MCAK)**: An atypical non-motile kinesin that uses ATP to bend protofilaments at both ends, acting as a potent **Catastrophe Factor**.
• **Katanin & Spastin**: AAA+ ATPases that sever microtubules internally.
pathology: Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia (HSP): Mutations in the SPAST gene (encoding the microtubule-severing ATPase Spastin) impair axonal microtubule remodeling in upper motor neurons, causing progressive lower-limb spasticity.
lab_workbench: Kymograph Analysis via Interference Reflection Microscopy (IRM) or EB1-GFP Live Imaging: Plots distance (x-axis) vs. time (y-axis) as a sawtooth triangle wave, where the upward slope gives polymerization velocity, the steep downward slope gives depolymerization velocity, and the peaks/valleys give Catastrophe and Rescue frequencies.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (3J6E — High-Resolution Cryo-EM Structure of GMPCPP vs GDP Microtubule Lattice)

node_myosin_motor.title: Myosin Superfamily (Myosin I, II & V) & The Lymn-Taylor Cycle
node_myosin_motor.subtitle: Actin-Based Mechanochemical ATPases | Lever-Arm Power Stroke & Processivity

metrics.directionality: Almost all Myosins (I, II, V) walk toward the Barbed (+) End; ONLY Myosin VI walks toward the Pointed (-) End!
metrics.myosin_ii_duty_ratio: Low duty ratio (~0.05; non-processive alone, operates in bipolar thick-filament ensembles)
metrics.myosin_v_step_size: High duty ratio (~0.7; processive hand-over-hand 36 nm steps matching F-actin helical repeat)

mechanism: Myosins consist of an N-terminal **Head (Motor) Domain** (binds F-actin and hydrolyzes ATP), a **Neck / Lever-Arm Domain** (binds calmodulin/light chains; amplifies conformational changes), and a C-terminal **Tail Domain** (dictates cargo binding or thick-filament dimerization).

THE 5-STEP MECHANOCHEMICAL CYCLE: (1) **Rigor State**: Head is tightly locked onto F-actin with zero nucleotide bound. (2) **ATP Binding**: ATP binds the motor pocket \rightarrow cleft opens and the myosin head **DETACHES** from actin! (3) **Cocking (Recovery Stroke)**: ATP is hydrolyzed to ADP + Pi (both remain bound), cocking the lever arm into a high-energy pre-stroke angle. (4) **Weak-to-Strong Rebinding**: Head binds a new actin subunit closer to the (+) end. (5) **Power Stroke**: Release of **Inorganic Phosphate (Pi)** triggers the forceful **Power Stroke** (lever arm swings ~5–10 nm), followed by ADP release to return to the Rigor state.
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR Exam Traps on the Myosin Cycle:
• **What causes Myosin to detach from Actin?** **ATP BINDING** (NOT ATP hydrolysis!). This explains *Rigor Mortis* after death when cellular ATP is depleted.
• **What triggers the mechanical Power Stroke?** The release of **Inorganic Phosphate (\text{P}_i$)** upon actin rebinding!

• **Directionality Exception**: Myosin I, II, and V move toward the **Barbed (+) end**; **Myosin VI** is the famous exception that moves backward toward the **Pointed (-) end** (used in clathrin endocytosis).

• **Myosin V Hand-Over-Hand Stepping**: Has an elongated neck binding 6 calmodulins per leg, allowing it to take huge **36 nm steps** (matching the exact 37 nm helical pitch of F-actin so it walks straight along one side of the filament without spiraling!).
pathology: Familial Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (HCM): Autosomal dominant missense mutations in MYH7 (encoding cardiac β-myosin heavy chain) cause hypercontractility, interventricular septal hypertrophy, and sudden cardiac arrest in young athletes.
Griscelli Syndrome: Mutations in MYO5A (Myosin Va) or Rab27a block melanosome transport along actin filaments in melanocytes, causing pigment dilution (silvery-gray hair) and neurological defects.
lab_workbench: FIONA (Fluorescence Imaging with One Nanometer Accuracy): Labeling a single calmodulin light chain on one leg of a Myosin V dimer with a fluorophore reveals alternating **72 nm / 0 nm** steps (while the center of mass moves 36 nm), proving the **hand-over-hand** (rather than inchworm) stepping mechanism!

node_kinesin_stepper.title: Kinesin Superfamily (Kinesin-1 to Kinesin-14)
node_kinesin_stepper.subtitle: Anterograde (+) End Microtubule Motors | 8 nm Hand-Over-Hand Neck-Linker Docking

metrics.canonical_direction: Plus (+) End Directed (Anterograde axonal transport from soma to synapse)
metrics.exception_direction: Kinesin-14 (e.g., Ncd in Drosophila) has a C-terminal motor domain and walks toward the Minus (-) End!
metrics.step_size: 8 nm per ATP hydrolyzed (Matches the exact length of one 8 nm α/β-tubulin dimer along a protofilament)

mechanism: Conventional **Kinesin-1** is a heterotetramer composed of two Heavy Chains (each with an N-terminal globular motor head, a flexible **neck linker**, and a coiled-coil stalk) and two Light Chains (which bind vesicular cargo or organelles like mitochondria and ER).

OPPOSITE NUCLEOTIDE COUPLING FROM MYOSIN: Whereas ATP binding detaches Myosin from actin, **ATP binding to the leading Kinesin head tightly locks it onto the microtubule** and causes its 14-amino-acid **Neck Linker** to zipper/dock forward, throwing the trailing ADP-bound head 16 nm forward to the next β-tubulin binding site (resulting in an 8 nm shift of the center of mass per 1 ATP hydrolyzed).
csir_high_yield: Motor Domain Position Dictates Directionality (CSIR Part B/C Rule):
• **N-terminal Motor Domain** (Kinesin-1, Kinesin-5/Eg5): Walks toward the **Plus (+) end**.
• **C-terminal Motor Domain** (Kinesin-14 / Ncd / Kar3): Walks backward toward the **Minus (-) end**!
• **Internal/Middle Motor Domain** (Kinesin-13 / MCAK): Diffuses to both ends and uses ATP to depolymerize microtubules (**Catastrophe Factor**).

Mitotic Bipolarity Motor (**Kinesin-5 / Eg5**): A homotetrameric bipolar motor with two pairs of (+) end motor heads at opposite ends of a rod; crosslinks antiparallel interpolar microtubules and slides them apart to push mitotic spindle poles away from each other!
pathology: Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 2A & Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia (SPG10): Mutations in KIF1B or KIF5A impair anterograde axonal transport of mitochondria and synaptic vesicles down meter-long motor axons, causing distal axonal degeneration.
lab_workbench: Single-Molecule Optical Tweezers (Optical Trap) Assay: A polystyrene microbead coated with a single Kinesin-1 dimer is held in an infrared laser beam above a microtubule; interferon-grade position tracking reveals discrete **8 nm steps** and a stall force of **~5–7 piconewtons (pN)**.

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (3KIN — Dimeric Kinesin Motor Domain Crystal Structure)
OMIM Database (KIF5A Mutations in Spastic Paraplegia & ALS)

node_dynein_dynactin.title: Cytoplasmic & Axonemal Dynein (AAA+ Minus-End Motors)
node_dynein_dynactin.subtitle: Retrograde (-) End Transport with Dynactin & 9+2 Ciliary Sliding Mechanics

metrics.directionality: Strictly Minus (-) End Directed (Retrograde transport toward Centrosome / Soma)
metrics.motor_architecture: Massive (~1.4–2 MDa) hexameric ring of 6 AAA+ ATPase domains (AAA1 is the primary catalytic site) + coiled-coil stalk
metrics.obligate_activator: Dynactin complex (p150Glued + Arp1 filament) + Cargo adaptors (BICD2 / Hook3)

mechanism: Unlike Myosin and Kinesin (which evolved from G-protein-like folds), **Dyneins** belong to the **AAA+ ATPase superfamily**—their motor domain is a giant wheel of six concatenated AAA+ modules (AAA1–AAA6) from which a 15 nm coiled-coil stalk projects a tiny Microtubule-Binding Domain (MTBD) at its tip.

1. **Cytoplasmic Dynein 1**: Requires the multi-subunit **Dynactin** complex (which contains a short filament of **Arp1** and a microtubule-binding **p150Glued** arm) plus a coiled-coil cargo adaptor to achieve long-range processive retrograde movement (carrying endosomes, lysosomes, and viruses toward the nucleus, and positioning the Golgi apparatus near the centrosome).

2. **Axonemal Dynein**: Permanently anchored by its tail to the **A-tubule** of one outer doublet in a 9+2 cilium/flagellum; its motor stalks walk toward the (-) end of the adjacent doublet's **B-tubule**. Because **Nexin (DRC)** links hold the doublets together, sliding force is converted into a rhythmic **bending wave**!
csir_high_yield: Classic Summers & Gibbons Trypsin Digestion Experiment (Guaranteed CSIR Part C Experimental Question):
• **Intact Flagellar Axonemes + ATP**: Undergo normal rhythmic **bending**.

• **Isolated Axonemes treated briefly with Trypsin (which cleaves the Nexin inter-doublet links and radial spokes) + ATP**: Instead of bending, the outer microtubule doublets **telescope / slide completely apart** up to 9x their original length! This proved that ciliary beating is driven by dynein-mediated inter-doublet sliding restricted by nexin crosslinks.
Golgi Positioning: Inhibiting Cytoplasmic Dynein causes the Golgi apparatus to fragment and disperse throughout the cytoplasm!
pathology: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia / Kartagener Syndrome: Autosomal recessive mutations in DNAH5 or DNAI1 (encoding axonemal dynein arms) immobilize respiratory cilia and sperm flagella, causing chronic sinusitis/bronchiectasis, male infertility, and **Situs Inversus** (50% chance of reversed left-right organ asymmetry due to immotile embryonic nodal cilia!).
Lissencephaly ('Smooth Brain'): Mutations in LIS1 (PAFAH1B1, a crucial regulator of cytoplasmic dynein) prevent neuronal migration during cerebral cortex development.
lab_workbench: Sodium Orthovanadate (\text{VO}_4^{3-}$) UV Photocleavage Assay: At micromolar concentrations ($10\ \mu\text{M}$), vanadate acts as a transition-state phosphate analog that selectively inhibits **Dynein** (at the AAA1 site) at concentrations that leave Kinesin and Myosin active!

external_resources.title: RCSB PDB (5NVU — Cryo-EM Structure of Human Cytoplasmic Dynein-1 bound to Dynactin and BICD2)
OMIM Database (DNAH5 Mutations in Kartagener Syndrome / Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia)

node_cell_cell_junctions.title: Cell–Cell Junctions: Tight, Adherens, Desmosomes & Gap Junctions
node_cell_cell_junctions.subtitle: Apical-to-Basal Epithelial Junctional Complex & \text{Ca}^{2+}$-Dependent Cadherin Mechanics

metrics.tight_junctions: Claudins & Occludins + ZO-1/2/3 scaffold -> Seal paracellular space & maintain apical/basolateral polarity
metrics.adherens_junctions: Classical Cadherins (E-Cadherin) + α/β/p120-Catenin -> Linked to Actin Microfilaments
metrics.desmosomes: Desmoglein & Desmocollin (Non-classical cadherins) + Plakoglobin/Desmoplakin -> Linked to Intermediate Filaments (Keratin)
metrics.gap_junctions: 6 Connexins = 1 Connexon (Hemichannel); 2 Connexons = 1 Gap Junction channel (<1.0 kDa permeability)

mechanism: From Apical to Basal along polarized epithelial cells, four specialized junctions coordinate tissue integrity:

1. **Tight Junctions (Zonula Occludens)**: **Claudins** and **Occludins** form anastomosing sealing strands that block paracellular solute leakage and act as a 'fence' preventing lipid/protein diffusion between apical and basolateral membrane domains.

2. **Adherens Junctions (Zonula Adherens)**: **Classical Cadherins** (E-, N-, P-cadherin) mediate **homophilic, \text{Ca}^{2+}$-dependent** trans-adhesion across the intercellular space, anchored intracellularly via **β-catenin** and **α-catenin** to the **Actin** belt.

3. **Desmosomes (Macula Adherens)**: Cadherin-family proteins **Desmoglein** and **Desmocollin** link via Plakoglobin and **Desmoplakin** to **Intermediate Filaments** (Keratin in epithelia; Desmin in cardiac intercalated discs) for extreme tensile strength.

4. **Gap Junctions**: Two hexameric **Connexon** hemichannels dock across a 2–4 nm gap to form an aqueous pore permeable to ions, \text{IP}_3$, cAMP, and metabolites $<1,000$ Daltons (gated closed by high cytosolic \text{Ca}^{2+}$ or low pH to quarantine dying cells!).
csir_high_yield: Why does EDTA + Trypsin dissociate cultured epithelial sheets into single cells? (CSIR Lab & Unit 4 Classic): **Cadherins** contain 5 extracellular cadherin (EC) repeats connected by rigid hinges that bind **\text{Ca}^{2+}$ ions**. Adding **EDTA** chelates \text{Ca}^{2+}$, causing cadherins to become floppy and protease-sensitive so Trypsin can cleave them!

Invertebrate Equivalents: Insects (Drosophila) lack tight junctions and instead use **Septate Junctions** to seal the paracellular barrier; Plants use **Plasmodesmata** (lined with plasma membrane and containing a central ER **desmotubule**) instead of gap junctions.
pathology: Pemphigus Vulgaris: Autoantibodies against **Desmoglein-3** (desmosomal cadherin) disrupt keratinocyte cell-cell adhesion (acantholysis), causing severe mucocutaneous blistering.

Epithelial-to-Mesenchymal Transition (EMT) in Cancer Metastasis: Transcription factors **Snail, Slug, and Twist** repress **E-cadherin** expression and upregulate **N-cadherin** ('Cadherin Switch'), allowing carcinoma cells to detach and invade.
lab_workbench: Lucifer Yellow Dye-Transfer Assay & TER (Transepithelial Electrical Resistance): Microinjecting Lucifer Yellow (~457 Da) tests Gap Junction coupling (stops if $>1$ kDa fluorescent dextran is used); Ohmmeter TER measurement quantifies Tight Junction paracellular barrier integrity.

node_integrin_focal_adhesion.title: Cell–Matrix Adhesion: Integrins, Focal Adhesions & Hemidesmosomes
node_integrin_focal_adhesion.subtitle: \alpha/\beta$ Heterodimeric RGD Receptors | Inside-Out & Outside-In Mechanotransduction

metrics.integrin_structure: Obligate Heterodimer of 1 α-subunit (18 types) + 1 β-subunit (8 types) = 24 mammalian Integrins
metrics.ligand_motif: Recognizes the tripeptide RGD (Arg-Gly-Asp) motif in Fibronectin & Vitronectin (requires divalent cations Mg2+/Mn2+)
metrics.focal_adhesion_link: Integrin (α5β1) + Talin/Vinculin/Paxillin/FAK -> Links ECM to Actin Stress Fibers
metrics.hemidesmosome_link: Integrin α6β4 + Plectin/BPAG1 -> Links Basal Lamina (Laminin-332) to Intermediate Filaments

mechanism: **Integrins** are transmembrane \alpha\beta$ heterodimers that physically and mechanically couple the Extracellular Matrix (ECM) to the intracellular cytoskeleton, operating in two conformational states: a bent, low-affinity **Inactive state** and an extended, high-affinity **Active state**.

• **INSIDE-OUT SIGNALING**: Intracellular signals (e.g., Rap1 GTPase in platelets or leukocytes) recruit **Talin** to bind the cytoplasmic tail of the $\beta$-integrin subunit, prying the $\alpha$ and $\beta$ tails apart and snapping the extracellular headpieces open to bind ECM ligands (like Fibronectin or Fibrinogen).

• **OUTSIDE-IN SIGNALING**: Binding of extracellular **RGD** motifs clusters integrins at **Focal Adhesions**, recruiting **Focal Adhesion Kinase (FAK)** and Src, which autophosphorylate (Tyr-397 on FAK) to activate PI3K/Akt survival pathways (preventing **Anoikis**—detachment-induced apoptosis).
csir_high_yield: Master Cell-Adhesion Matching Table for CSIR NET Part B & C:
• **Adherens Junction** = Cell–Cell | **Cadherin** | Links to **Actin**.
• **Desmosome** = Cell–Cell | **Desmoglein/Desmocollin** | Links to **Intermediate Filaments**.
• **Focal Adhesion** = Cell–Matrix | **Integrin** (\alpha_5\beta_1$) | Links to **Actin** (via Talin/Vinculin/FAK).
• **Hemidesmosome** = Cell–Matrix | **Integrin** (\alpha_6\beta_4$) | Links to **Intermediate Filaments** (via Plectin).

• **Selectins** (L-, E-, P-selectin): Mediate transient \text{Ca}^{2+}$-dependent **leukocyte rolling** by binding sialyl-Lewis-X carbohydrates on endothelial mucins, followed by **ICAM-1 binding to \beta_2$-Integrin (LFA-1)** for firm arrest and extravasation!
pathology: Leukocyte Adhesion Deficiency Type 1 (LAD-1): Autosomal recessive mutation in ITGB2 (encoding the \beta_2$ integrin subunit CD18) prevents neutrophils from firmly adhering to vascular endothelium and extravasating to infection sites, causing severe recurrent bacterial infections with ZERO pus formation and marked leukocytosis.
Glanzmann Thrombasthenia: Genetic deficiency of platelet Integrin \alpha_{IIb}\beta_3$ (gpIIb/IIIa) prevents fibrinogen crosslinking and platelet aggregation.
lab_workbench: Synthetic Soluble RGD Peptide Competition Assay: Adding soluble Arg-Gly-Asp (RGD) tripeptides (or snake venom disintegrins) to cultured fibroblasts competitively blocks Integrin-Fibronectin binding, causing cells to round up and detach from the culture dish!

node_ecm_collagen_matrix.title: The Extracellular Matrix: Collagen Triple Helix, GAGs, Fibronectin & Basal Lamina
node_ecm_collagen_matrix.subtitle: (Gly-X-Y)n Vitamin C Hydroxylation, Proteoglycan Hydration Gels & Laminin/Type IV Networks

metrics.collagen_repeat: (Gly–X–Y)n where X = Proline and Y = 4-Hydroxyproline or 5-Hydroxylysine
metrics.glycosaminoglycans: Repeating disaccharides (Uronic acid + Amino sugar); Hyaluronan is the ONLY non-sulfated, non-protein-bound GAG!
metrics.basal_lamina_core: Type IV Collagen sheet + Laminin (αβγ cruciform heterotrimer) + Nidogen/Entactin + Perlecan

mechanism: 1. **COLLAGEN (Tensile Strength)**: Most abundant protein in mammals (~25% of total protein mass). Three left-handed \alpha$-chains wind around each other into a right-handed superhelical **Triple Helix**. Every 3rd residue MUST be **Glycine** (the only amino acid small enough for its -H side chain to fit inside the crowded central axis of the triple helix!). **Prolyl 4-hydroxylase** (requiring **Ascorbate / Vitamin C** and \alpha$-ketoglutarate to keep active-site \text{Fe}^{2+}$ reduced) hydroxylates proline residues to form interchain hydrogen bonds that stabilize the triple helix at 37°C. Secreted as soluble **Procollagen** (with N- and C-propeptides preventing premature intracellular aggregation), cleaved extracellularly into **Tropocollagen**, and covalently crosslinked by copper-dependent **Lysyl Oxidase**.

2. **PROTEOGLYCANS & GAGs (Compressive Resistance)**: Core proteins (like **Aggrecan** in cartilage) covalently attached (via a Xylose-Gal-Gal-GlcUA tetrasaccharide linker on Serine) to negatively charged sulfated **Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs)** (Chondroitin sulfate, Keratan sulfate, Heparan sulfate). Dense \text{SO}_4^{2-}$ and \text{COO}^-$ negative charges attract \text{Na}^+$ counterions and massive amounts of water, creating a turgid hydrogel that resists compression.

3. **FIBRONECTIN & LAMININ (Adhesive Glycoproteins)**: **Fibronectin** is a disulfide-linked C-terminal dimer containing modular Type I, II, and III repeats (Type \text{III}_{10}$ houses the **RGD** sequence). **Laminin** is a cross-shaped heterotrimer (\alpha\beta\gamma$) that self-assembles with **Type IV Collagen** (non-fibrillar sheet) to form the **Basal Lamina**.
csir_high_yield: High-Yield ECM Facts Repeatedly Tested in CSIR NET:

• Why must Procollagen propeptides be cleaved ONLY AFTER secretion? If N- and C-propeptides were cleaved inside the ER/Golgi, insoluble collagen fibrils would polymerize prematurely inside the cell and rupture the secretory pathway!

• **Hyaluronic Acid (Hyaluronan) Exception**: Unlike all other GAGs (Chondroitin, Dermatan, Keratan, Heparan sulfate), Hyaluronan is **completely NON-SULFATED**, is **NOT covalently attached to a core protein**, and is synthesized directly at the **plasma membrane** (by Hyaluronan Synthase) rather than in the Golgi!

• **Elastin Crosslinking**: Hydrophobic elastin monomers (Tropoelastin) are crosslinked via Lysine residues into rare tetrafunctional **Desmosine** rings (by Lysyl Oxidase), allowing arteries and lungs to recoil like rubber bands.
pathology: Connective Tissue & ECM Genetic Disorders:
• **Scurvy (Vitamin C Deficiency)**: Defective Prolyl Hydroxylase lowers the melting temperature (T_m$) of collagen below 37°C, causing gum bleeding and fragile blood vessels.
• **Osteogenesis Imperfecta ('Brittle Bone Disease')**: Point mutations replacing a single **Glycine** in Type I Collagen (COL1A1/COL1A2) stall triple-helix zippering.
• **Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome**: Mutations in Type III/V Collagen or Procollagen N-peptidase (hypermobile joints, hyperextensible skin).
• **Alport Syndrome**: Mutations in **Type IV Collagen** (\alpha_5$ chain) disrupt the glomerular basement membrane (hematuria + sensorineural deafness).

• **Marfan Syndrome**: Mutations in **Fibrillin-1** (FBN1, which forms microfibril sheaths around elastin and sequesters latent TGF-β) cause tall stature, arachnodactyly, lens dislocation, and aortic aneurysm.
lab_workbench: Gelatin Zymography (MMP-2 / MMP-9 Assay): SDS-PAGE gels copolymerized with gelatin (denatured collagen); after renaturation in Triton X-100 and incubation with \text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Ca}^{2+}$, Matrix Metalloproteinases (MMPs) digest the gelatin, appearing as clear unstained bands against a Coomassie-blue background (inhibited by **TIMPs** or EDTA).

agents.name: Cytochalasin D (Fungal Alkaloid)
agents.mechanism_of_action: Binds specifically to the fast-growing Barbed (+) end of F-actin filaments
agents.rescue_experiment: Classic CSIR NET Experiment: Caps the barbed (+) end while allowing subunit loss from the pointed (-) end, depolymerizing F-actin. In dividing cells, nuclear division (mitosis/karyokinesis via microtubules) completes normally, but the contractile ring fails to form—blocking cytokinesis and creating binucleated cells!

agents.name: Latrunculin A (Red Sea Sponge Toxin)
agents.mechanism_of_action: Binds 1:1 in the nucleotide cleft of monomeric G-Actin, preventing polymerization
agents.rescue_experiment: Drops free polymerizable [G-Actin] below C_c^+$, causing rapid depolymerization from BOTH ends of all dynamic actin filaments.

agents.name: Phalloidin (Death Cap Mushroom Toxin)
agents.mechanism_of_action: Locks adjacent F-actin subunits laterally and longitudinally (blocks Pi release & depolymerization)
agents.rescue_experiment: Drops k_{\text{off}}$ to near zero, freezing F-actin filaments and halting treadmilling! Because cell migration requires both assembly AND disassembly (turnover), Phalloidin completely paralyzes amoeboid cell motility.

agents.name: Colchicine / Nocodazole / Vinblastine
agents.mechanism_of_action: Binds unpolymerized α/β-tubulin heterodimers, preventing curved-to-straight transition

predicted_phenotype.mitotic_spindle_tension: Collapsed (Spindle Assembly Checkpoint Arrest in M-Phase)

agents.rescue_experiment: Prevents tubulin addition to the (+) end, triggering catastrophe and dissolving the mitotic spindle. Cells arrest at Metaphase via Mad2/BubR1 Spindle Assembly Checkpoint (used clinically in karyotyping to accumulate metaphase chromosome spreads!).

agents.name: Taxol (Paclitaxel — Pacific Yew Bark)
agents.mechanism_of_action: Binds the luminal side of polymerized β-tubulin inside intact microtubules (ignores free dimers)

predicted_phenotype.mitotic_spindle_tension: Frozen (Cannot generate anaphase depolymerization force -> M-Phase Arrest!)

agents.rescue_experiment: CSIR High-Yield Paradox: Even though Colchicine depolymerizes microtubules and Taxol hyper-stabilizes them, BOTH drugs arrest dividing cancer cells at Metaphase! Why? Because anaphase chromosome segregation requires dynamic instability (both polymerization AND depolymerization) to satisfy the Spindle Assembly Checkpoint.

agents.name: Blebbistatin (Myosin II) & Monastrol (Kinesin-5 / Eg5)
agents.mechanism_of_action: Blebbistatin locks Myosin II in weak-actin-binding ADP·Pi state; Monastrol blocks Kinesin-5 bipolar sliding
agents.rescue_experiment: Monastrol inhibits Kinesin-5 (Eg5) without affecting microtubules themselves, preventing centrosome separation and creating a hallmark 'monoaster' monopolar spindle; Blebbistatin selectively blocks non-muscle Myosin II contractility and cytokinesis.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the 10 nm cytoskeletal filament network that binds ZERO nucleotides (no ATP/GTP) and has ZERO associated motor proteins because its antiparallel tetramer subunit is apolar.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Correct! Intermediate Filaments assemble from antiparallel staggered tetramers, making both ends chemically identical (apolar) so directional motors cannot walk on them.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the Level 2 node contrasting the nucleator that stays at the pointed (-) end to make 70° branches versus the FH2-ring nucleator that rides the barbed (+) end to make straight filaments.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Spot on! Arp2/3 nucleates 70° branched actin networks from the (-) end in lamellipodia, whereas Formins processively track the growing (+) end to build unbranched cables.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the AAA+ ring motor protein that requires Dynactin for retrograde (-) end transport and whose mutation in 9+2 axonemes causes Kartagener syndrome (immotile cilia + situs inversus).
quiz_challenges.explanation: Exact match! Dynein is a minus-end-directed AAA+ motor; axonemal dynein drives ciliary sliding, while cytoplasmic dynein drives retrograde axonal transport.

quiz_challenges.prompt: Click the α/β heterodimeric cell-matrix adhesion hub that recognizes RGD motifs in Fibronectin and links to actin stress fibers at focal adhesions via Talin and Vinculin.
quiz_challenges.explanation: Correct! Integrins mediate bidirectional cell-ECM signaling and anchor to actin (at focal adhesions) or intermediate filaments (at hemidesmosomes via α6β4).
